successors.name: Dahomey
successors.text: Whydah, 'conquered by King Agaja of the Kingdom of Dahomey' in 1727

ledger.x: c. 1580: the Kingdom of Whydah begins (timeline 'c. 1580-1728'); the infobox says 'Established: 17th century' and the origins section that it 'became independent in the late 17th century'; King Agbangla, the third king, is attested in the 1680s. The page does not say from whom it became independent.
1702 (May): Akwamu seizes Whydah and makes it tributary.
1727 (February): the Akwamu tie ends with Dahomey's conquest.
1727: the fighting ends in Dahomey's conquest.
1727: the Kingdom of Whydah ends on the mainland; 'The state formed a refugee dynasty on offshore islands after the Dahomeyan invasion around 1727.'

wars.name: Dahomean conquest of Whydah
wars.outcome: Dahomey won: Whydah conquered in 1727; the exiled dynasty's attempts to return ended by 1734 (Agaja page).
